defect: R36 originally used a consent fingerprint containing server-generated reservation IDs and occurred_at as the convergence key. R37 generates those values anew on every HTTP attempt, so one authenticated action could fork into multiple reservations after a network retry.
correction: Reservation uniqueness and convergence now use previous workspace, stable subject and the R37 authenticated request fingerprint. New transport IDs and time converge on the first accepted reservation.
preserved: the full consent fingerprint remains stored for receipt integrity
exact consent-ID replay still requires the same request fingerprint
the old erased scope remains unchanged
R38 still consumes one consent once
next_gate: Design the dormant server adapter with an explicit reserve-then-create recovery state so a timeout between R36 and R38 resumes the first reservation rather than issuing new authority.
not_authorized: creating an application caller or Edge Function entrypoint
